protocol_deviations: The issue's suggested use of store.project_state for committed nodes was adapted: project_state stores nodes in the {"id", "value"} wrapper shape while the coordinator's values mapping holds bare values, so resume replays the committed SUCCEEDED deltas directly (same deterministic projection, unwrapped) — this is also what makes REVISE/RETIRE corrections reconstruct exactly.

W5 recovery re-executes the worker instead of adopting the stored RESULT_RECEIVED (the design doc's optimization). This is the issue's sanctioned at-least-once worker semantics and keeps a single uniform resume path; the duplicate RESULT_RECEIVED is not an audit violation and the last one is authoritative.

W6 (VALIDATION_PASSED committed without the SUCCEEDED batch) is not distinguished from W5: the resumed step re-appends VALIDATION_PASSED before the SUCCEEDED batch. Audit truthfulness only forbids VALIDATION_PASSED combined with FAILED, so the run stays clean; a dedicated revalidation-only path was judged out of the pragmatic subset.

W3's idempotency-key query against an external system is deferred (no external-system cooperation exists); the DISPATCHED payload already carries run_id:invocation_id so effectful workers can dedup on their side.

Program identity on resume is enforced via the RUN_STARTED payload's recorded program/version plus per-step task-text matching; a renamed but structurally identical program is refused by the former, while a same-name program with identical step ids/commands would resume (accepted limitation, documented in solution.md).
The resume CLI accepts an optional --workspace like run (superset of the issue's flag list) so effectful commands resume with the same workspace policy as run.
Issue #11 ran concurrently on src/tikhon/registry/ and tests/test_registry.py; no edits were made in those trees and the combined suite is green (484 passed).
